evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose +10.5 points over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trend for the same period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses the -70 threshold (currently -71.4), it signals a material return of public-transport commuting that drives increased foot traffic to retail outlets near transit hubs within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -70 (less negative than -70)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -75.0 to -71.4 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses the -70 threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility interact to produce a compounding effect on RETAIL_REC, as commuters both travel to work and pass through retail corridors, amplifying retail recovery beyond what either series predicts alone over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show consistent weekly improvement over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no greater than the additive effect predicted from WORKPLACES-only and TRANSIT-only trends, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both rising.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening-roadmap regime where RESIDENTIAL mobility is declining and WORKPLACES is rising simultaneously, eased capacity limits and travel restrictions cause an immediate one-week uptick in RETAIL_REC as pent-up demand is released.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.6 to 16.4 while WORKPLACES rose from -41.1 to -30.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week despite RESIDENTIAL falling and WORKPLACES rising concurrently.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.3 to -13.6 (+6.7) between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the two weeks following a PARKS jump exceeding the 5-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The onset of Southern Hemisphere spring brings longer daylight and improving weather, which independently of policy changes drives a gradual rise in both outdoor activity and discretionary retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -37.3 to -35.6 over the last three weeks alongside fluctuating PARKS gains
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show a sustained increase over four weeks despite the seasonal spring transition, remaining flat or declining.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week after both the WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL thresholds are met simultaneously.
